data.text: A **Higher-Order Component (HOC)** is a function that takes a component and returns a new component with additional props or behavior. It is a powerful pattern for **reusing component logic** across multiple parts of your application without repeating code.

Think of an HOC as a **wrapper** around your component. The HOC receives the original component, adds some functionality, and returns an enhanced version. The original component remains untouched, which keeps your code clean and predictable.

terms.definition: A function that takes a component and returns a new component with enhanced capabilities. It is not a component itself, but a component factory.
The process of placing a component inside an HOC to transform or augment its behavior and props.
A static property set on the enhanced component to help React DevTools show a meaningful name instead of 'Anonymous' or 'ForwardRef'.
The technique of passing additional props from the HOC into the wrapped component that the original component did not receive directly.

data.text: Both HOCs and Render Props solve the same problem: **sharing logic between components**. However, they use very different approaches. Use the comparison below to decide which pattern fits your use case.

cards.title: Higher-Order Component
cards.description: Wraps a component to inject props and behavior automatically.
pros: Declarative usage - looks like a normal component
Easy to apply to many components at once
cons: Can cause wrapper hell when nesting many HOCs
Static methods must be manually copied
Props can be harder to trace in DevTools

cards.title: Render Props
cards.description: Passes a function as a prop to control rendering dynamically.
pros: Explicit control over what gets rendered
Easy to access shared state in render
cons: Can be harder to read with many render props

data.title: Naming Your HOC
data.text: Prefix HOC names with **with** followed by the behavior they add: `withAuth`, `withLogger`, `withTheme`. Always set a `displayName` so React DevTools can show meaningful names for your enhanced components.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: HOCs are functions that take a component and return an enhanced component
They enable logic reuse without modifying the original component
Use the `with` prefix for naming and always set `displayName`
HOCs inject props and can add any cross-cutting concern
data.takeaway: HOCs are component factories that let you reuse logic across your app.

data.title: Create a withAuth HOC
data.description: Build a `withAuth` Higher-Order Component that wraps a protected page component and redirects unauthenticated users to the login page.
steps: Create a `withAuth` function that accepts a component and returns a new component
Use a mock `useAuth` hook inside the HOC to check authentication status
If the user is not authenticated, redirect them to `/login`
If authenticated, render the wrapped component with all original props
Set a `displayName` on the returned component for debugging
data.expectedOutcome: A working `withAuth` HOC that protects any component from unauthenticated access.
